criteria.description: The repo exists at ~/development/codebase-map as a git repository (git init, no remote) with a README that documents the external verifier venv path /Users/mattli/.venvs/codebase-map/bin/python and the pytest command used to run tests.
criteria.verifyBy: Check ~/development/codebase-map/.git exists and `git -C ~/development/codebase-map remote` is empty; grep the README for the string '/Users/mattli/.venvs/codebase-map/bin/python' and a pytest invocation.

criteria.description: A scan function walks a target repo and returns an in-memory result where each included file records at least: relative path, line count, content hash, and a source-vs-test classification exposed as a stable enumerable value/flag.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest builds a temp repo, calls the scan function, and asserts each entry exposes path, line_count, content_hash, and a source/test classification; run via /Users/mattli/.venvs/codebase-map/bin/python -m pytest -q.

criteria.description: Line counting is crude and language-agnostic (counts physical lines without parsing), producing deterministic counts for known fixture files including the edge cases: trailing-newline, no-trailing-newline, empty file, and blank-lines-only file.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest writes fixtures for (a) content with a trailing newline, (b) content with no trailing newline, (c) an empty file (assert the pinned expected count, e.g. 0), and (d) a file of only blank lines, and asserts each reported line_count equals its pinned expected value.

criteria.description: Content hashing is stable: identical file content yields the same hash across runs, and changed content yields a different hash.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest hashes the same content twice (equal), then mutates one byte and asserts the hash differs.

criteria.description: The scanner respects real .gitignore semantics — not substring matching — including anchored patterns, directory-only patterns, nested .gitignore files in subdirectories, negation/re-include, and vendored dirs like .venv/ and node_modules/, so ignored paths are absent while re-included paths are present.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest constructs a temp repo whose root .gitignore contains an anchored pattern (e.g. /foo), a directory-only pattern (e.g. build/), entries for .venv/ and node_modules/, and a negation re-include (e.g. !keep.py); plus a nested .gitignore in a subdirectory with its own pattern. Scan and assert: files under .venv/, node_modules/, build/, the anchored /foo, and the nested-ignored path are ABSENT, while a non-ignored source file AND the negated-re-included keep.py are PRESENT. (Matching may be delegated to git itself or a real gitignore-semantics library.)

criteria.description: The scanner skips binary files (detected via a NUL-byte heuristic) and an enumerated set of lockfiles, excluding them from the scanned source set.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest creates a file containing NUL bytes and lockfiles named package-lock.json, yarn.lock, poetry.lock, and Cargo.lock in a temp repo, scans, and asserts every one of these is excluded from the scanned files while an ordinary text source file is included.

criteria.description: Files are classified as source vs test via path/filename heuristics, and the result totals source files and test files separately by count (separate line totals may be provided additionally).
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest creates files with test-indicating names/paths (e.g. test_*.py, *_test.py, *.test.ts, files under a tests/ dir) and normal source files, scans, and asserts each is classified correctly and that separate source-count and test-count totals are computed.

criteria.description: A snapshot writer serializes the scan result to a JSON snapshot under ~/.codebase-map/<repo-name>/ and never writes into the analyzed repo; the JSON round-trips back to an equivalent structure, and the analyzed tree is left byte-for-byte unchanged.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest points the output dir at a temp location (and/or asserts the derived path is under ~/.codebase-map/<repo-name>/ and outside the target), writes a snapshot, reads it back, and asserts loaded data equals written data (path, line_count, hash, classification, totals preserved). Before scanning, record the full file listing + contents of the temp target repo; after scan+snapshot, assert no file anywhere under the target tree was created, modified, or deleted.

criteria.description: Scan output is deterministic: two scans of the same unchanged tree produce equal snapshot data with stable entry ordering, so later deltas are not flaky.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest scans the same temp repo twice (or writes two snapshots) and asserts the serialized snapshot data (including entry ordering) is equal across both runs.

criteria.description: The full hermetic test suite passes under the pinned interpreter.
criteria.verifyBy: Run /Users/mattli/.venvs/codebase-map/bin/python -m pytest -q in ~/development/codebase-map and observe all tests pass with no failures/errors.

scope.description: All new code lives in the new repo at ~/development/codebase-map; do not modify voice-tutor, dev-harness, ~/.voice-tutor/, or any existing repo.
This sprint is the pure scan + snapshot layer only: no LLM/summarization, no HTML rendering, and no delta/drift computation (those are later sprints).
Scanning any real target must be strictly read-only; all output goes under ~/.codebase-map/<repo-name>/, never into the analyzed repo.
Do not create a .venv/ inside the repo; tests use the external pinned interpreter /Users/mattli/.venvs/codebase-map/bin/python.
